comparison: Both address theoretical modeling claims (C61, C62, C63). OpenEval finds the modeling mathematically sound and supportive of the mechanism, while peer reviewers express uncertainty about temporal logic (whether Gwl inactivation precedes PP2A-B55 reactivation) and whether the mechanism is rapid enough for mitotic exit.

Both address exclusion of Fcp1 as pEndos phosphatase (C64-C70). OpenEval finds the evidence comprehensive and convincing with multiple converging lines of evidence. Peer reviewers accepted this negative result without challenge, indicating agreement.

Both address identification of PP2A-B55 as the pEndos phosphatase using genetic, biochemical, and purification approaches (C3, C13, C14, C22, C23, C28, C33, C34, C36 overlap). OpenEval finds the convergence of evidence strongly supportive. Peer reviewers did not explicitly challenge the identification but raised methodological concerns about assay linearity, lack of replicates, and appropriateness of Michaelis-Menten kinetics for analyzing inhibited complexes.

Both address protein concentration estimates and stoichiometry (C56, C57, C58 overlap; peer also includes C59, C60, C75). OpenEval finds the Western blot quantitation and mass spectrometry data supportive of the 5:1 Endos:PP2A-B55 ratio. Peer reviewers explicitly questioned whether stoichiometry measurements are sufficient, requesting direct measurement of pEndos to PP2A-B55 ratios in mitosis to validate the model.

Both address kinetic measurements of Km values (C4, C5 overlap; peer also includes C19, C39, C40, C47, C48, C71-C73). OpenEval finds the kinetic measurements robust despite technical challenges. Peer reviewers questioned the appropriateness of applying Michaelis-Menten kinetics to a strongly-bound inhibited complex and noted inconsistencies in inhibitor sensitivities between experiments.

Both address active site competition and IC50 measurements (C47-C52 overlap). OpenEval finds evidence for active site competition strong based on okadaic acid competition and dose-response data. Peer reviewers questioned whether dephosphorylation within the complex would be independent of dilution and whether the kinetic framework is appropriate.

Both address auto-reactivation mechanism (C53, C54, C55). OpenEval finds the in vitro reconstitution experiments directly demonstrate the mechanism with well-controlled time-course data. Peer reviewers raised concerns about whether the kinetic framework is valid and whether the mechanism is rapid enough for mitotic exit.

Both address differential biochemical properties (C19, C20, C21 overlap). OpenEval finds these properties consistently observed and later explained by kinetic differences. Peer reviewers accepted these observations without challenge.

Both address established background knowledge (C1, C2, C6-C12 overlap; peer also includes C74, C76-C80). OpenEval notes these are appropriately cited prior work providing essential context. Peer reviewers accepted these background claims without challenge.

OpenEval R6 addresses inhibitor profiling (C15-C18) finding the experiments systematic with appropriate controls. Peer R1 includes these claims (C15, C17, C18) but raises broader methodological concerns about assay linearity and lack of replicates that apply to this data.

OpenEval R8 addresses systematic exclusion of alternative phosphatases (C24-C27, C32). Peer R1 includes these claims among the broader identification evidence but raises methodological concerns about single-point measurements without variation estimates.

OpenEval R9 addresses Mono-Q chromatography separation (C35, C37, C38). Peer R1 includes these claims as part of the PP2A-B55 identification evidence but raises concerns about methodological rigor and use of asynchronous cells.

OpenEval R14 addresses control experiments demonstrating specificity (C29-C31). Peer R1 includes these claims in the broader identification evidence but raises methodological concerns about lack of replicates.

OpenEval R10 addresses differential inhibitor sensitivities with purified enzyme (C39, C40). Peer R2 includes these claims and questions inconsistencies in inhibitor sensitivities between experiments and validity of the kinetic framework.

OpenEval R16 addresses explanation of differential inhibitor sensitivities based on enzyme kinetics (C71-C73). Peer R2 includes these claims but questions whether the kinetic framework is appropriate for this system.

OpenEval R15 addresses quantitative parameters from literature and measurements (C59, C60, C74, C75). Peer R4 includes concentration claims (C59, C60, C75) and explicitly questions whether stoichiometry measurements are sufficient to validate the model.
OpenEval R17 addresses literature context on Inhibitor-1/PP1 system (C76-C80). Peer R8 includes these as accepted background claims providing conceptual framework without challenge.
